newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia seeks jail for riot trial defendants.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia seeks jail for riot trial defendants.

text.p: Indonesian state prosecutors sought sentences of 14 weeks' jail for 44 supporters of ousted party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri on trial in connection with riots in Jakarta last July, newspapers reported on Friday.

Prosecutors asked during a Thursday hearing for a sentence of two months against another defendant because he was over 60 years old, while charges against four other people would be dropped, the Jakarta Post said.

It said that since the defendants had been held since July 27, the time already spent in custody would be deducted from their sentences. There was no indication when the three-judge panel would announce their verdict.
Under charges filed, the defendants face a maximum nine years in jail.
Another 75 defendants, also Megawati supporters, are being tried in a separate session in the Jakarta Central District Court. Altogether 124 defendants are on trial.
They were all charged with assault and disobeying police orders after a police-backed raid on the central Jakarta headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) in July.
They had occupied the headquarters in protest against the ousting of Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, as PDI leader by a government-backed faction.
Following the raid, demonstrators took to the streets of central Jakarta, looting and burning buildings and vehicles in the worst violence the city had seen in more than two decades.
The officially-appointed National Commission of Human Rights said in its final report on the riots that five people died and 23 were still missing.
Defence lawyers have complained of discrimination by police in that only Megawati supporters had been arrested.
